channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: Russian strikes kill 26 in Ukraine after longest ceasefire ends
item.description: Russia killed at least 26 people in strikes on a village in southern Ukraine on Monday, including civilians collecting humanitarian aid, emergency workers and police officers. The attack came hours after a rare ceasefire ended, extinguishing hopes of progress towards peace.

item.title: AI 'highly likely' to be used in attack on Britain's infrastructure
item.description: Artificial intelligence is "helping to industrialise cyber attacks" and is "highly likely" to be used in attacks on Britain's critical national infrastructure by 2028, the National Cybersecurity Centre (NCSC) has warned.

item.title: North Korea denies involvement in Binance hack, criticizes FBI probe
item.description: North Korea has denied its involvement in the recent cryptocurrency heist at Binance, dismissing as “a trite provocation” a U.S. announcement that North Korean hackers were behind the incident

item.title: New York state reports 1st measles-associated death in over 30 years
item.description: A child died in Lewis County associated with the ongoing measles outbreak, health officials said.

item.title: North Korea rejects US allegations over $6 billion Binance crypto heist
item.description: North Korea on Tuesday dismissed US allegations that it was behind a $6 billion cryptocurrency theft from Binance as "absurd rhetoric", accusing Washington of seeking to portray the country as a cybercriminal state and warning that US hostility could affect future diplomatic engagement.

item.title: Midterm elections live updates: SCOTUS denies Trump bid to segregate California votes
item.description: The Supreme Court denied the Trump administration's request for an injunction ordering California to segregate 20,000 ballots that could have been cast by noncitizens.

item.title: Emergency alerts hacking 'designed to undermine trust in government', expert says
item.description: Emergency alert systems in Russia and Ukraine were hit in cyber attacks overnight, with fake warnings of possible nuclear strikes broadcast to users in both countries. The systems have since been brought back under control, though much remains unclear about the attacks, including who was responsible. FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney speaks with Dr Melanie Garson, Associate Professor in International Security at University College London. She says that these kind of attacks "are designed to undermine faith in the government's ability to provide trust".

item.title: Trump promised 'no more wars'. His foreign policy tells another story
item.description: Donald Trump promised an “America First” foreign policy and pledged to keep the US out of foreign wars. But since returning to the White House, his administration has been deeply involved in conflicts around the world. From the war in Ukraine and threats to Greenland and Canada, to the US intervention in Venezuela, Trump's shifting approach to the Middle East and war with Iran, Vedika Bahl examines his foreign policy record since returning to office.

item.title: Uganda withdrawing troops from peacekeeping mission in Somalia
item.description: In tonight's edition, Uganda starts drawing down troops just days after the UN ends its political mission in Somalia. Also, upcoming municipal elections in South Africa risk solidifying growing political fragmentation. And the drought gripping Chad could be the country’s worst in more than 40 years.

item.title: How do midterm candidates plan to fight inflation? Economists evaluate proposals
item.description: Proposals include tax cuts and an end to the Iran war.

item.title: The Long Hull: Karl Bushby reflects on perseverance & 'best of humanity' on his 28-year journey home
item.description: “They say it takes a village. In this case, it took a world.” After 28 years and some 50,000 kilometres, British explorer and adventurer Karl Bushby has returned to his hometown of Hull, completing an extraordinary life journey across four continents that illustrates not only the limits of human endurance, but also the intricate relationship between individual determination, geopolitical constraints and a world of humanity. Speaking to France 24's François Picard shortly after his emotional homecoming, Bushby reflects on an undertaking that resembles a modern-day Odyssey, although the defining obstacles were often more geopolitical than mythological.

item.title: EU says fridge attacks 'deliberate attempt to disrupt' bloc's food supply
item.description: Grocery stores from Sweden to Portugal were hit Monday by a suspected cyberattack on their freezer systems, in what the EU denounced as a deliberate attempt to disrupt the bloc's food chain. Supermarkets in Belgium, Estonia, Finland, Ireland, Luxembourg and the Netherlands were among at least eight countries affected in the incident, which came three weeks after a cyberattack caused mass disruption in French grocery stores. Food retailers were forced to throw out produce that had spoiled or was at risk of spoiling after refrigerator temperatures soared overnight. FRANCE 24's Dave Keating reports from Brussels.

item.title: What you need to know about the Election Day Voter Poll
item.description: The Election Day Voter Poll helps answer the question of who won and why and explain what issues were important in the election.

item.title: AI chatbots are becoming political advisers. Their answers can mislead voters
item.description: Millions of Americans are turning to AI for election information, but chatbots are getting voting facts wrong and recommending candidates, raising concerns they could influence voters' decisions.

item.title: Is America really that polarized? The answer might be a surprise
item.description: The U.S. has become more politically polarized, but research shows people overestimate their differences and there is 'messy middle' majority of Americans who share overlapping political views.

item.title: Free and fair? The Midterms and the state of US democracy
item.description: How far will the president of the United States press this time if Tuesday’s Midterm elections don’t go his party’s way? From “only if the Republicans win” campaign promises to a US Justice Department that’s already gotten involved in races, will the White House weigh on the outcome? How will ballot counting go? What’s changed since his “stop the steal” rhetoric begat the January 6th, 2021 storming of the US Capitol?

item.title: MAGA: Why Trump's most loyal supporters are turning against him?
item.description: Is Trump losing the support of the very coalition that brought him back to power? Just one day before the midterm elections, Trump's approval rating stands at 32%, one of the lowest ever recorded at this stage of a presidency. And discontent is growing beyond Democratic voters. Some of Trump's most loyal Republican and MAGA supporters are increasingly torn between political loyalty and economic reality. The war in Iran, rising costs linked to the Strait of Hormuz blockade, unfulfilled “America First” promises and other controversial issues, including the Epstein files scandal, are widening the rift between Trump and his electoral base. Can he regain control of the diverse coalition that makes up MAGA? FRANCE 24 journalist Stella Elgersma spoke to MAGA and Republican experts to explore how the movement has evolved, what its supporters want and what is driving their discontent. Watch the full youtube documentary : https://youtu.be/XkehRG77itY?si=iOfIl0PwrgyX-j0X

item.title: Israeli 'unity government': Efrat Shapira expects Herzog will urge rival camps to form a 'coalition'
item.description: Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Efrat Shapira Rosenberg, Israeli Radio/TV Host, Columnist, Podcaster and Educator. Following a deadlocked Israeli election, “everyone is saying who they’re not going to sit with, but no one is actually saying who they will sit with.” As President Isaac Herzog prepares to consult parliamentary factions over the formation of a new coalition, the impasse reveals tensions that extend beyond the familiar confrontation between Benjamin Netanyahu and his political opponents. According to Shapira, co-host of the highly popular Israeli politics podcast Miflaget Hamakshavot, the divisions are equally pronounced within the opposition bloc supporting Gadi Eisenkot.

item.title: LIVE: ABC News Live
item.description: 24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events

item.title: Judge accuses DOJ of 'weaponization,' tosses case against ex-FBI officials
item.description: The judge said he was "deeply troubled" by the mistakes and rushed nature of the case over the FBI's Hunter Biden probes — one of several politically charged DOJ actions ahead of the midterms.

item.title: Two teens arrested after five boys stabbed at Halloween party
item.description: Two boys have been arrested after five teenagers were seriously injured when they were allegedly stabbed at a party on Halloween.

item.title: Trans row nurse Sandie Peggie loses discrimination case against union
item.description: The Royal College of Nursing (RCN) did not discriminate against one of its members because of her gender beliefs, a tribunal has ruled.

item.title: French student protests: 'Illiberal' Macron govt dismisses social movement as 'urban violence'
item.description: Jennie Shin is pleased to welcome Éric Fassin, Sociologist and Professor at Université Paris 8. “In a democracy, elections are very important, but it’s not the end of democracy. It’s the beginning,” explains Fassin. He interprets France’s student protest movement growing into a challenge to socioeconomic policy and what he describes as an “illiberal turn” in government. Connecting the treatment of working-class, racialized youth with wider restrictions on dissent, he argues that racism and democratic participation are central to understanding the unrest. His analysis also challenges the attribution of responsibility to the left, placing the government’s response within a broader debate over the normalization of oppressive measures and the far right.

item.title: Burnham will 'reshape Commonwealth' as he joins King in Caribbean
item.description: The prime minister has said the UK will play a leading role reshaping the Commonwealth, including pursuing a debt "reset" to help nations struggling with higher borrowing costs.

item.title: Trump says deal with Tehran 'could happen' amid 'intensive' talks
item.description: Tehran on Monday said that the country was holding "intensive" indirect talks with Washington to avoid a fresh round of US attacks on Iran ahead of the US midterm elections this week. Foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei shared Iranian plans to reopen blockaded energy corridor, the Strait of Hormuz, if the US were to meet its demands.

item.title: Refrigeration cyberattacks highlight risks of connecting industry to the internet
item.description: Cyberattacks affecting supermarket refrigeration systems on Monday in several European countries – including Belgium, Estonia, Finland, Ireland, Luxembourg, the Netherlands and Sweden – have highlighted the risks of connecting industrial infrastructure to the internet.

item.title: Iran offers deal on Hormuz Strait, Netanyahu wants to 'finish the job'
item.description: Iran said Monday it had a two-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and resume nuclear talks with the United States, shortening a process originally expected to take seven days. Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said he wanted to "finish the job" first. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Angela Diffley has more.

item.title: Petition to ban French right-wing TV channel clears 600,000 signatures after racist killing
item.description: A petition calling for right-wing television channel CNews to be taken off-air cleared 600,000 signatures on Monday after a Frenchman shot and killed a French national of Congolese origin and wounded seven others. The 39-year-old shooter is believed to have been an avid watcher of CNews, which is owned by ultra-conservative billionaire Vincent Bolloré and has been accused of promoting far-right anti-immigrant views.

item.title: British adventurer arrives back at mother's home after 28-year journey
item.description: British adventurer Karl Bushby enjoyed an emotional reunion with his mother and family on Monday, as he arrived back home after a 28-year, 50,000-kilometre trek from South America, crossing four continents on foot.

item.title: Iconic Paris department store BHV Marais granted bankruptcy protection
item.description: A French court granted bankruptcy protection on Monday to iconic department store BHV Marais, which has stood in central Paris for around 170 years. The move comes after the company announced last week that it sought bankruptcy protection to safeguard its operations and jobs as part of a "relaunch".

item.title: The Supreme Court rejects a DOJ push to separate California ballots
item.description: The U.S. Supreme Court has denied a last-minute request from the Department of Justice to wade into its unprecedented feud with California over the state's voter rolls.

item.title: What changes if Democrats win a majority in Congress?
item.description: Americans head to the polls on Tuesday for the US midterm elections, which could flip the majority in one or both houses of Congress from the Republicans to the Democrats. What would a Democratic majority mean for the country's political landscape, and how might Democrats move to keep President Donald Trump in check?

item.title: WATCH: Seahawks inspire young leaders beyond the field
item.description: ABC News' Kayna Whitworth reports live from Lumen Field in Seattle on how the Seahawks are helping kids build leadership skills and pursue their dreams.

item.title: A musical overview of trans-European punk
item.description: This week on arts24, we're bringing you a double dose of European punk. Elias Bender Rønnenfelt is a singer with Copenhagen's finest post-punk export, Iceage. The group is currently touring Europe, and he is stopping off in Paris this week to play the Pitchfork festival solo. We also welcome Chris Hughes from Fat Dog. Born in South London in 2020 during lockdown, Fat Dog have just released their second album "Cancel Me (I'm Tired)", which will thrill synth lovers and punk rockers alike. They are currently touring France and Europe.

item.title: Israel's president begins process of coalition government negotiations
item.description: Israel's President Isaac Herzog begins the process of coalition government negotiations this week. One possibility is for the centrist opposition bloc to form a government with the Arab parties, which would oust current Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Protests for and against such a coalition this weekend made it clear the Israeli public is divided over the idea.

item.title: Scientists begin tests on human composting, an eco-friendly alternative to burials and cremation
item.description: Humans have caused irreversible changes to our planet in their time on Earth, pollution that continues even in death. Cremation relies heavily on fossil fuels, while traditional burials take up land. So is there a more eco-friendly way to honour our loved ones? French scientists are exploring the possibility of composting human bodies, a process that returns those who have died to the earth. Our Down to Earth team reports.

item.title: Nine dead in small plane crash near Trump's Florida home
item.description: Nine people were killed Sunday when the Learjet they were travelling in plummeted into a neighbourhood in southern Florida, just miles from US President Donald Trump's resort home of Mar-a-Lago, officials said.

item.title: WATCH: Video of ICE agent apparently pointing gun in bystander's face during arrest
item.description: ICE is facing new scrutiny over a video that allegedly shows an ICE agent pointing a gun in the face of a bystander in California.

item.title: FIFA to share documents relating to World Cup sell-off plan
item.description: FIFA will give members of its ruling council access to some documents for the first time related to the World Cup sell-off, Sky News understands.

item.title: Democratic Rep. Stevens endorses GOP candidate Mike Rogers in Michigan US Senate race
item.description: Stevens and Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed have feuded publicly recently over a campaign ad Stevens said was anti-Semitic.

item.title: WATCH: A look at the state of the midterm races
item.description: ABC News' Senior Political Correspondent Rachel Scott breaks down the state of play as a new New York Times/Siena poll shows Democrats are gaining ground, slightly pulling ahead in key Senate races.

item.title: WATCH: Sisters go from lifesaving surgery to running a marathon
item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to cancer survivor Kate Stevens, who received a bone marrow transplant from her sister and, around two decades later, ran a marathon with her.

item.title: Major business group calls for fundamental change in UK-EU relationship
item.description: A major UK business group has called on the government to "fundamentally reassess" the country's relationship with the EU, as it said the current system is still "failing to deliver".

item.description: What happens in California could shape how America taxes the superrich. But will its billionaire tax fill state coffers — or drain them?

item.title: Voters are concerned as healthcare costs increase. Here are some possible causes
item.description: As many U.S. voters worry about healthcare costs, experts tell ABC News there are many reasons why costs may be rising.

item.title: 'Everything is destroyed': Hackers target refrigerators in new cyber attacks
item.description: Cyber hackers have targeted fridges and freezers in supermarkets in several European countries including Ireland – causing temperatures to increase and food to spoil.

item.title: Advocates rally voters after dozens of polling sites closed in 'swing' Texas county
item.description: Community and advocacy groups in Tarrant County, Texas, are rallying to get voters to the polls after officials shut down dozens of polling locations before the midterms.

item.title: How does this fluoride-free toothpaste compare when it comes to oral health?
item.description: Many people are swapping out their fluoride dental products for ones made with a mineral called hydroxyapatite. What do dentists say about it?

item.title: With students scarce, college admissions offices get friendlier, less intimidating
item.description: Colleges are trying to transform an admissions process that has often been daunting, secretive and stressful into an experience that's open, easier — and downright friendly.

item.description: Sweden's Andreas Almgren won his first men's NYC marathon, and Kenya's Shelia Chepkirui won her second NYC marathon.

item.title: British backpackers in Australia could face changes to visa rules
item.description: British backpackers in Australia could be forced to spend more time in regional areas under proposed changes to the country's working holiday visa.

item.title: Suspected far-right activists from Britain 'with tear gas bombs' detained in France
item.description: Five suspected far-right activists from Britain were detained in northern France last Thursday, according to authorities.

item.description: While the spotlight will be on the nearly 60,000 people running the course, they would not be there without the help of thousands of volunteers on the sidelines.

item.description: The King will speak about slavery with "unflinching honesty" and "sincere sorrow" in a speech to Commonwealth leaders amid increasing pressure for Britain to offer an apology over its role in the transatlantic slave trade.

item.description: A Yemeni staff member of the UN Human Rights Office has died in Houthi custody after being arbitrarily held for more ​than two years, the UN human rights chief has said.

item.description: A US judge has dismissed President Donald Trump's lawsuit against The Wall Street Journal over a story about a birthday card he allegedly sent Jeffrey Epstein.

item.description: Around 90% of stolen cryptocurrency assets following a hack on a major exchange has been replenished, according to Binance.

item.description: A man has died following an attack at a centre housing migrants in Ireland.

item.description: Body camera footage shows the dramatic police shootout that left a suspected sailboat thief dead in Newport, Rhode Island. The 40-foot boat was stolen back in August.
